recentItems.title: Max Mara presents collection inspired by adventurous women
recentItems.description:
(24 Sep 2026) 
ASSOCIATED PRESS
Milan - 24 September 2026
1. Pan down on exterior venue 
2. Various backstage
3. SOUNDBITE (English) Ian Griffiths, designer: 
"The idea of the Max Mara show this spring is the idea of ‘utility lux.' There is a great deal of discussion at the moment about the luxury market, but for us the word is used sometimes lazily to mean something that is very expensive and doesn't really perform any real function. But Max Mara clothes do perform a function. They empower you. You put them on in the morning and you are equipped for your day."
4. Medium shot Ian Griffiths being interviewed
5. Pan down Max Mara inspiration board with photos of aviators
6. Close-up Chiara Ferragni entering the show
7. Medium of Chiara Ferragni posing
8. Medium of Kelly Rutherford posing
9. SOUNDBITE (English) Kelly Rutherford, actor: 
"It’s just so classic. I mean, we love it obviously. It is so easy to wear and comfortable and feminine, it’s beautiful."
10. Kelly Rutherford posing
11. SOUNDBITE (English) Kelly Rutherford, actor - on current projects: 
"I don’t know, just getting my kids into university right now and moving, so we are dealing with that but everything else good, just I'll be going to Paris, which will be fun. Yeah."
12. Medium of Adria Arjona posing
13. Wide pan of the show room
14. Various of Im Yoon-ah (Yoona)
15. Various of Ami and Aya Suzuki
16. Medium of Keiko Kitagawa
17. Medium of Leighton Meester talking to the media
18. SOUNDBITE (English) Leighton Meester, actor:
 "To celebrate and - I don't know -see all the fabulous looks. I really love Milan as well and Milan Fashion Week. So I am really excited, I'm excited to see everything and I really love - not to brag - I love my outfit today. So yeah, I just think it’s like such a beautiful and interesting show."
19. Wide of front row
20. Medium of front row including Gao Ye and Im Yoon-ah
21. Various of catwalk show
22. Various of final pass
23. Outside shot with people leaving the show and heading to next
24. SOUNDBITE (English) Colleen Barry, The Associated Press:
"We are here at the Max Mara show where now some of the celebrity guests have now exiting. The collection was inspired by the likes of Amelia Earhart with a sense of adventure. There were aviator glasses and utility jackets. The silhouette was long and lean, even when the pants were wider and there were also some gauchos, the waist was always cinched. The house is aware that not everyone can go for a full monochrome look, so they did a little black and white, which is unusual to see here. some of the celebrity guest included co-stars Leighton Meester and Kelly Rutherford from 'Gossip Girl.'"
25. Wide shot guests leaving

STORYLINE:
The Max Mara silhouette for next summer is long and lean, even when trousers are roomy they are cinched tightly at the waist. 

The latest collection - show in Milan on Thursday - took inspiration from adventurous women, like aviator Amelia Earhart, with references seen in aviator glasses and utility pockets on vests, jackets and trousers. 

While the brand hewed closely to its monochrome ethos there were also looks that paired dark chocolate and black garments with white - a move by Max Mara’s designer Ian Griffiths to invite women to mix and match. 

Dresses were tightly fitted ribbed knits, while elongated trenches added a touch of elegance to wide-legged pants, including gauchos.

 A sheer jumpsuit over a ribbed bodysuit brought a sense of daring utility. 

Front row guests included "Gossip Girl" co-stars Leighton Meester and Kelly Rutherford.

recentItems.title: Latest Russian strikes kill two people in Kyiv as the UNGA debates how to end the war
recentItems.description:
(24 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY: 

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Kyiv, Ukraine - 24 September 2026 
1. Various of destroyed private houses and premises
2. SOUNDBITE (Russian) Hasan Khalyov, 64, Kyiv resident:
++OVERLAID BY 1, 3 AND 4++
"Exactly at 1 a.m., there was a ball of fire and everyone was hiding, everything was falling down. This is a nightmare, simply a nightmare."
3. Close of a destroyed private house, tilt down to rubble
4. Close of destroyed house 
5. SOUNDBITE (Ukrainian) Liubov Pazuk, 74, Pensioner:
++OVERLAID BY SHOTS 6-8 ++
“Over these years, we have learned how to cope. We don’t get used to it, we adapt, because we have only one choice: to stay here, on our land, despite everything,  we simply pull ourselves together because our only choice is to remain here, on our land, despite everything. Perhaps those enemies, those Russian scumbags, want to force us to flee and say, ‘fine, let Putin come.’ But we do not want Putin here. It’s all right; we will patch things up. Maybe they will give us some plastic sheeting, or perhaps we will cover the windows with pillows. It is not freezing yet. We will endure.”
6. Mid of crater, tilt up to destroyed house
7. Mid of resident searching through rubble
8. Mid of damaged house
9. Tilt down of debris
10. Mid of car under rubble
11. Wide of damaged house
STORYLINE:
Two people were killed, and eight others were injured in a Russian strike on Kyiv on Thursday.

The overnight attack damaged more than 50 civilian sites, including residential buildings, post offices, a maternity hospital and a textile plant, authorities said.

The home of 76-year-old Liubov Pazuk was damaged in the strike. She said the electricity went out and everything began to fall around her.

“We don’t get used to it; we adapt, because we have only one choice: to stay here, on our land, despite everything,” Pazuk told The Associated Press.

Pazuk said she was preparing for a harsh winter but that nothing could weaken her determination to endure.

“We will not starve, and we will not freeze either. Everything will be fine. The most important thing is that our people do not change and continue to believe that what matters most to us is our land - the land beneath our feet,” she said.

Kyiv resident Hasan Khalyov said the attack began at about 1 a.m.

“Everything was falling around us. It was a nightmare,” he said.

Khalyov recalled an attack on a power plant last year that left residents without electricity or heating. He said he expected this winter to be even harsher.

“We survived somehow, but this winter will probably be much worse than the last. This is simply destruction - and for what?” he said.

AP Video shot by Srdjan Nedelikovic

recentItems.title: El ejército colombiano patrulla una ciudad turística en la primera operación militar bajo el mandato
recentItems.description:
(24 Sep 2026) 
COLOMBIA Seguridad SP
Source: ASSOCIATED PRESS
No additional restrictions beyond those terms outlined in your license agreement.
Video de AP grabado por Marko Alvarez.

El ejército colombiano patrulla una ciudad turística en la primera operación militar bajo el mandato del presidente De la Espriella.

——————————————————————————————————————
ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Santa Marta, Colombia - 23 de septiembre de 2026 
1. Diversas tomas de soldados patrullando las calles 
2. Oficial de pie en unas escaleras 
3. Soldados subiendo a una camioneta 
4. SOUNDBITE (Español) Gral. José Perdomo, comandante de la Primera División del Ejército de Colombia en Santa Marta: 
++PARTE SUPERPUESTA CON TOMAS 2,3,5++ 
“En desarrollo de la Operación Santa Marta, hemos fortalecido el despliegue operacional para proteger a la población y anticiparnos a cualquier intención de los grupos armados organizados que afectan la seguridad y tranquilidad de los ciudadanos en Santa Marta y su zona metropolitana. Para ellos hemos dispuesto el empleo permanente de tropas de fuerzas especiales”.  
5. Soldados registrando a un motociclista 
6. Puesto de control militar 
7. Diversas imágenes de personal del ejército brindando seguridad en las calles y a las afueras de supermercados
8. SOUNDBITE (Español) Antonio Ochoa Díaz, residente de Santa Marta: 
++PARTE SUPERPUESTA CON TOMAS 6, 7, 9++ 
“Más que todo la ley de acá es la de los grupos, y la gente por miedo hace caso y eso. Ahora que esta el ejército caminando por ahí, cuidando pues uno se siente  , más seguro también. Eso es solamente digo yo máximo una semana. Ya después se van, y  queda otra vez la ciudad y los barrios igual”.
9. Diversas imágenes de negocios cerrados debido al paro armado decretado por grupos ilegales en la zona
10. SOUNDBITE (Español) María Margarita Guerra, gobernadora del departamento del Magdalena: 
++PARTE SUPERPUESTA CON TOMAS 11,12,13,14++
“Tenemos que cambiar la historia. Siento que aquí tenemos que unirnos, aquí los buenos somos más, como seres humanos claramente, cuidándonos, si claro, para eso esta la policía, esta el ejército, se han aumentado a mas de 1.500 hombres en el distrito de Santa Marta. El señor presidente ha traído a policiales y ejército de todo el país”.
11. Militares vigilando
12. Policías cuidando negocios
13. Policías llevando a dos detenidos
14. Diversas Tomas de la playa en la ciudad de Santa Marta 
15 Tomas de una carretera con un autobús quemado

STORYLINE:
Las calles de Santa Marta, uno de los principales destinos turísticos de Colombia, lucían inusualmente desiertas el miércoles tras una orden presidencial de militarizar la ciudad en un intento por contrarrestar la violencia de un grupo armado. 

El miedo se había apoderado de la ciudad caribeña el día anterior, después de que al menos tres vehículos fueran incendiados —incluidos un taxi y un autobús de transporte público— y los comerciantes recibieran amenazas, en algunos casos por parte de hombres armados que los intimidaron a plena luz del día. 

Los pocos supermercados abiertos estaban custodiados por policías armados. "Ahora que esta el ejército caminando por ahí, cuidando pues uno se siente más seguro también”declaró a The Associated Press el taxista Antonio Ochoa Díaz.

La gobernadora del Magdalena, María Margarita Guerra, caminaba por un mercado público animando a la gente, “Tenemos que cambiar la historia", afirmó.




Video de AP grabado por Marko Alvarez

ANNE MARIE GARCIA, ASSOCIATED PRESS

recentItems.title: Lebanese in Beirut criticise Netanyahu ahead of UNGA address, fear another escalation in war
recentItems.description:
(24 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Beirut, Lebanon - 24 September 2026
1. Tilt down from Lebanese flag to traffic in Beirut 
2. Various of traffic
3. Lebanese flag 
4. Various of building destroyed by Israeli strike 
5. Various of Naeem Salah, local resident reading newspaper 
6. SOUNDBITE (Arabic) Naeem Salah, resident and newspaper vendor: 
“As for Netanyahu and the people behind him, they have elections, so he takes advantage of every opportunity or occasion to show his people that he is a national hero for the Jewish people, of course. And don’t think that he has any mercy, because he is capable of doing this. There are people who support him and people who give him guidance. What is called the 'deep state' in America is all under his command, whether through support with weapons or money."
7. Street 
8. SOUNDBITE (Arabic) Naeem Salah, resident and newspaper vendor: 
“Fear is present across all of Lebanon. Don’t think it’s only in the south. Israel is carrying out operations there. What is happening in the south… they want to force people to leave, to carry out a transfer, like in Palestine. And in the coming days, what can I tell you? The destruction they are causing is turning the land into scorched earth. I mean, there is an occupation."
9. Beirut skyline
10. Pedestrians walking
11. SOUNDBITE (Arabic) Boutros Matar, Beirut resident:  
"Certainly, there will be an escalation, especially because there are elections coming up in Israel. There will be elections in Israel in about a month or a month and a half. The war in Lebanon is connected to the Israeli elections. It’s not out of the question. And as for their aggression, whether there are elections or not, they are aggressive anyway. But certainly, there will be greater escalation."
12. Various of Beirut coastline
13. SOUNDBITE (Arabic) Ezzat Kraytem, Beirut resident: 
“This is Netanyahu. What can we expect from him? There is no logic when it comes to Netanyahu. Anything is possible, whether it’s a reaction or no reaction, or whatever might happen. Here in this country, we live day by day waiting to see what Trump and Netanyahu will do."
14. Various of destroyed building
STORYLINE:
Residents in Beirut voiced growing anxiety over the possibility of further escalation between Israel and Lebanon’s Hezbollah group, saying they fear the conflict could intensify in the coming weeks amid continued Israeli military operations in southern Lebanon.

Their comments on Thursday came ahead of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s speech at the United Nations General Assembly.

Beirut newspaper vendor Naeem Saleh said many Lebanese are worried about the trajectory of the conflict and believe the threat extends beyond the country's southern border region.

Saleh added that fear is felt across Lebanon, not only in the south, where Israeli operations have continued. He said many people are concerned that the ongoing military campaign and destruction could force residents from their homes and further deepen displacement.

"The destruction they are causing is turning the land into scorched earth. I mean, there is an occupation," said Saleh.

The comments reflect concerns among many Lebanon residents as regional tensions remain high and fears persist that hostilities could expand following months of cross-border exchanges and military operations.

For Beirut residents, uncertainty over the future of the conflict has left them worried about security and stability.



AP video by Fadi Tawil

recentItems.title: A peep inside the village centre healing Ireland's sick or injured bats
recentItems.description:
(24 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Bruree, County Limerick, Ireland - 24 September 2026:
1. Wide aerial of village ++MUTE ++
2. Wide of woman entering bat rehabilitation centre
3. SOUNDBITE (English) Susan Kerwin, Founder, Bat Rehabilitation Ireland: ++SOUNDBITE OVERLAID ON SHOTS 4-7++
“It was during the pandemic, the COVID pandemic, that I really pushed and started it as a charity and pushed for loads of publicity on it. Just because of the COVID pandemic, bats were being villainised and they were made out to be the cause of this pandemic. I was getting calls every day from members of the public that were absolutely terrified. They didn’t want bats roosting close to their house, there was people that were threatening to use expanding foam and block them in there, threatening to kill the bats, burn them out of different buildings that they were in, and it was just horrific to me.”  
4. Close up of Soprano pipistrelle bat held in gloved hands
5. Close of bat in gloved hands
6. Close of spreading a bat’s wing with aluminium ring visible
7. Various of feeding bat with mealworm
8. Wide pan of bat ambulance van turning into driveway
9.  SOUNDBITE (English) Susan Kerwin, Founder, Bat Rehabilitation Ireland: ++SOUNDBITE OVERLAYED ON SHOT 8, 10-12++
“When bats arrive into care, they are host to a number of different ectoparasites. We collect samples of these and we send them to university here in Ireland. They’re then tested to see the micro-organisms that they are carrying and also pathogens that they are carrying. This then gives us an overall idea or picture of the health of our own bats here in the wild in Ireland.”   
10. Close of bat's head poking out of hands
11. Close of ectoparasites (skin surface parasites) in test tube
12. Close of screen showing ectoparasites under a microscope
13. Close of of thumb stroking bat
STORYLINE:
This is the village of Bruree in County Limerick in the west of Ireland.

The village and its woodlands are home to bat populations.

Looking out for them is Susan Kerwin from Bat Rehabilitation Ireland.

She says they're one of the world’s most misunderstood and maligned animals.

Kerwin founded the charity during the COVID pandemic.

"Bats were being villainised and they were made out to be the cause of this pandemic. I was getting calls every day from members of the public that were absolutely terrified," she says. 

The charity cares for bats from across the Irish Republic’s twenty-six counties.

They arrive either injured, underweight or separated from their mothers.

Bat Rehabilitation Ireland has a team of around 50 volunteers around the country to help collect injured or orphaned bats.

In 2023, they crowdfunded a specially equipped bat ambulance to help them reach remote areas not covered by volunteers.   

When bats first arrive at the rehabilitation centre, they are examined for parasites which are removed and placed in test tubes.

Kerwin and her colleagues then send these off to Galway University for further study.

AP video by Rory Byrne

recentItems.description:
